title: Lobar pneumonia in HIV (CD4 480): Streptococcus pneumoniae
vignette: A 34-year-old man with HIV comes to the emergency department due to fever, chills, productive cough, and left-sided chest pain that worsens with deep breathing. His symptoms began 3 days ago and have progressively worsened. The patient was diagnosed with HIV 4 years ago during routine screening, and he takes antiretroviral therapy. His CD4 count was 480 cells/mm3 a month ago. Temperature is 38.8 C (102 F), blood pressure is 110/66 mm Hg, pulse is 110/min, and respirations are 22/min. Physical examination shows dullness to percussion, bronchial breath sounds, and crackles over the left lower lung. The right lung and cardiac auscultation findings are normal. Laboratory testing reveals an elevated leukocyte count with left shift. Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible for this patient's current symptoms?

clues.text: left-sided chest pain that worsens with deep breathing
clues.note: Pleuritic chest pain with acute fever/productive cough over a few days suggests a typical bacterial lobar pneumonia.
A relatively PRESERVED CD4 count (480; >200) makes opportunistic infections (PCP at CD4 <200, disseminated fungal at <50) far less likely; typical bacteria predominate.

clues.text: dullness to percussion, bronchial breath sounds, and crackles over the left lower lung
clues.note: Dullness, bronchial breath sounds, and crackles indicate LOBAR CONSOLIDATION - classic for Streptococcus pneumoniae.

whatMatters: Acute lobar pneumonia (fever, productive cough, pleuritic pain, focal consolidation, leukocytosis) in an HIV patient with a relatively PRESERVED CD4 (480) = STREPTOCOCCUS PNEUMONIAE - the most common cause of community-acquired pneumonia in HIV-infected and uninfected people alike (and HIV increases invasive pneumococcal risk). Answer G.
strategy: Use CD4 to gate the differential: at CD4 480 (>200), think TYPICAL bacterial pneumonia -> S pneumoniae (lobar consolidation, acute onset). Reject opportunistic/atypical causes that need low CD4 or fit a different tempo: Aspergillus (CD4 <50, cavitary), Pneumocystis (CD4 <200, subacute diffuse dyspnea, reticulonodular), TB (weeks, upper-lobe cavitary), Legionella (GI/neuro, atypical), Mycoplasma (young, mild 'walking pneumonia'), and influenza (viral, not lobar bacterial consolidation).

eliminations.label: Aspergillus - CD4 <50, cavitary
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: invasive aspergillosis (angioinvasive mold). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it affects severely immunosuppressed patients (CD4 <50) with nodular/cavitary infiltrates, not a lobar pneumonia at CD4 480. ✅ Correct if: profound immunosuppression with a cavitary/nodular lesion (halo sign).

eliminations.label: Influenza - viral, not lobar consolidation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: influenza virus (acute fever, myalgias, malaise). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: influenza is not a lobar bacterial consolidation; lobar findings suggest bacterial (often secondary) pneumonia. ✅ Correct if: viral prodrome without focal consolidation (or secondary bacterial pneumonia).

eliminations.label: Legionella - atypical, GI/neuro
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: Legionella (atypical pneumonia). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it usually has prominent GI symptoms (diarrhea), confusion, hyponatremia, and poorly Gram-staining sputum; S pneumoniae is more common overall. ✅ Correct if: pneumonia + watery diarrhea + confusion + hyponatremia.

eliminations.label: Mycobacterium tuberculosis - weeks, upper-lobe cavitary
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: reactivation TB. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: TB is subacute/chronic (weeks) with cough, weight loss, night sweats, and UPPER-lobe cavitary disease - not a 3-day lobar lower-lobe pneumonia. ✅ Correct if: chronic cough with upper-lobe cavities/hemoptysis.

eliminations.label: Mycoplasma - young, mild 'walking pneumonia'
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: Mycoplasma (atypical pneumonia). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes a milder, subacute illness with patchy interstitial infiltrates, not acute lobar consolidation with high fever. ✅ Correct if: young patient with mild cough +/- cold agglutinins.

eliminations.label: Pneumocystis jiroveci - CD4 <200, subacute diffuse
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: PCP (opportunistic fungus). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: PCP occurs at CD4 <200 with WEEKS of progressive dyspnea, dry cough, hypoxia, and bilateral reticulonodular infiltrates - not acute lobar pneumonia at CD4 480. ✅ Correct if: CD4 <200 with diffuse infiltrates and exertional hypoxia.

reasoning: Acute fever, productive cough, and pleuritic pain with focal lobar consolidation and leukocytosis = typical bacterial pneumonia
The CD4 count is relatively preserved (480 > 200), making opportunistic infections unlikely
Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common cause of community-acquired pneumonia regardless of HIV status
mechanism: Although HIV impairs cell-mediated immunity, it also reduces OPSONIZING antibody production and phagocyte recruitment, so HIV patients are at markedly increased risk for INVASIVE BACTERIAL infections with ENCAPSULATED organisms - especially STREPTOCOCCUS PNEUMONIAE. S pneumoniae is the MOST COMMON cause of COMMUNITY-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA in both HIV-infected and uninfected people, presenting acutely with fever, productive cough, PLEURITIC chest pain, LEUKOCYTOSIS, and signs of LOBAR CONSOLIDATION (dullness to percussion, bronchial breath sounds, crackles). The risk of invasive pneumococcal disease is elevated in HIV REGARDLESS of CD4 count, and all HIV patients should receive PNEUMOCOCCAL VACCINATION. The other organisms are far less likely here: opportunistic infections (Pneumocystis at CD4 <200, Aspergillus at CD4 <50) require low CD4; TB is chronic/cavitary; and Legionella/Mycoplasma/influenza have atypical or viral presentations that don't fit acute lobar consolidation. A relatively preserved CD4 of 480 further points away from opportunistic pathogens.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro/Pulm > CAP in HIV: S pneumoniae most common (encapsulated; increased invasive risk regardless of CD4); lobar consolidation; use CD4 to gate opportunistic infections (PCP <200, Aspergillus/CMV/MAC <50); vaccinate.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Lobar pneumonia + CD4 480 = typical bacteria -> S pneumoniae (most common CAP).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on lobar consolidation, CD4 thresholds, encapsulated organisms, or opportunistic vs typical pneumonia? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: PCP/Aspergillus need low CD4; TB is chronic/cavitary; Legionella/Mycoplasma/influenza are atypical/viral (not acute lobar).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: S pneumoniae = most common CAP in HIV and non-HIV; lobar consolidation; increased invasive risk regardless of CD4.

keywords.back: Increased invasive disease regardless of CD4; vaccinate

firstAid.detail: Micro: most common CAP; lobar consolidation; HIV increases invasive risk.
Micro > PCP <200, Aspergillus <50; TB chronic; atypicals differ.

memoryHook: CD4 is a healthy 480 and the lung is solidly consolidated - no exotic bug needed: it's plain old pneumococcus, the #1 pneumonia in everyone.
